narrative.overview:
A cool daylight laboratory where the work is laid out as specimens: one large halftone figure at a time, a great deal of air, no frames and no night. The ground is a blue-grey white (not cream), the ink is blue-black, and a single cold ultramarine marks the one thing that is current. The site's own code draws every figure as a field of dots, so the dots are the material of this world, not decoration on top of it.

Density is low and the scale is wide: a name set light at up to 400px sits against a calm plate, and lists are made of large names, not cards. Structure comes from hairlines and from tonal steps between ground and well, never from boxes, radii or shadows. Dark exists as an opt-in bench (slate with a pale periwinkle accent) that the visitor chooses; daylight is the default for everyone.

This replaces the earlier Observatory system (dark warm night, orange signal, Commissioner, viewfinder brackets). None of its devices carry over.

The scene pages (Gargantua, Space 3D) and the 404 are always on the dark bench, using its ink #e6ecef and signal #8ea2ff.
keyCharacteristics: Daylight by default; dark only by the visitor's stored choice.
One accent, ultramarine, used sparingly: lead dots of a plate, the current link, primary actions, the current-item underline.
Light-weight (300) Geologica at very large sizes; Onest for reading; mono for readouts only.
Zero radius, hairline borders, no shadows.
Halftone dot plates read --ink and --signal from the page, so they follow the theme.

rules.name: The One Current Thing Rule
rules.body: Ultramarine marks what is current or actionable (the active link, the active index name, the lead dots, the primary action). It is never a fill for decoration and never spread across a surface.

rules.name: The Token Parity Rule
rules.body: Every page reads colour through --ground, --panel, --well, --line, --line-strong, --ink, --ink-muted, --signal, --on-signal, --signal-ink set on body while a .page is mounted. Canvas drawings read the same variables; do not hard-code colours in a plate or a page.

rules.name: The Light At Scale Rule
rules.body: Display type is weight 300 with tight negative tracking; weight rises (600) only at 22px and below. Never bold a display line.

rules.name: The Readout Only Rule
rules.body: Mono is for values, coordinates, tags and contact strings. Headings and running text never use it.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are not lifted with box-shadow. The only box-shadows in the shared system are inset underlines marking the current nav link (1px) and the current language (2px).

dos: Do start from daylight (#eef1f2) and treat dark as the visitor's stored opt-in.
Do keep every radius at 0 and every border at 1px hairline.
Do read colours from the page tokens, in CSS and in canvas drawings.
Do set display type at weight 300 with negative tracking, and let it be very large.
Do pair every new name list or figure with a single large plate, not a grid of small ones.
Do keep both languages equal: Geologica and Onest carry Cyrillic; check long Russian words with overflow-wrap.
Do put the dark-bench tokens on scene pages and keep the same ink and signal pair in canvas dot fields.
Do give long reading a measure: one column of at most 740px, text at 18/30 near 66ch, and a contents list in the margin that disappears when there is no margin.
donts: Don't use a dark room, warm cream, orange signal, Commissioner, or viewfinder brackets; these belong to the retired Observatory.
Don't add shadows, glows or rounded corners.
Don't box the header, language toggle, theme button, contact rows or footer; they are unboxed text on hairlines.
Don't frame a card: no panel fill, border or radius around AI, Games or Spirit entries.
Don't put a frame, border or card around a dot plate.
Don't use a second accent colour, or ultramarine as a large fill.
Don't use mono for headings or running text.
Don't render a section of six small plates where one big plate can morph.
